script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. LOS ANGELES NIGHT STREETS - NIGHT

A LONELY SILHOUETTE of a MAN, MIKE, walks through the night streets of Los Angeles. A heavy rain falls on the pavement, creating a soothing rhythm.

Mike, mid-forties, disheveled, wears a raincoat. He carries an old, worn briefcase.

INT. MIKE'S APARTMENT - LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Mike enters his dimly lit apartment. He sits at his desk, opens his briefcase, and begins to write on a notepad.

MIKE
(Mumbling to himself)
This is it. I've got it. The perfect story.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Mike sits at a table in a crowded coffee shop. He meets JESSICA, a young woman in her late twenties, who is also a writer. They strike up a conversation.

JESSICA
(Smiling)
I love your raincoat. It's very literary.

MIKE
(Laughs)
You're too kind. It's just old and worn, like me.

Jessica laughs and shares her own struggles as a writer. They bond over their shared passion for storytelling.

INT. MIKE'S APARTMENT - EVENING

Mike calls his EX-WIFE, LUCY, to make amends for past wrongs.

MIKE
(Hesitant)
Lucy, I know I've hurt you. I want to make things right.

LUCY
(Angrily)
What makes you think I want to talk to you?

MIKE
(Determined)
I've been thinking about our past. I realize now that I've been holding on to anger and resentment. I want to let go and move forward.

INT. ART GALLERY - DAY

Mike attends an art gallery opening where he runs into ANNA, a former high school classmate who he's always had a crush on. They catch up, and Mike learns that Anna has forgiven her own past wrongdoers.

ANNA
(Wistfully)
Forgiveness is a powerful thing. It allows us to heal and move forward.

INT. MIKE'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Mike writes late into the night, inspired by his encounters with Jessica, Lucy, and Anna. He finally completes his story, a tale of forgiveness.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Mike and Jessica meet again at the coffee shop. He shares his completed story with her. She's moved by the theme of forgiveness and offers to help him publish it.

EXT. LOS ANGELES NIGHT STREETS - NIGHT

Mike walks through the night streets, no longer lonely, as the rain falls around him. He feels a sense of peace and closure.

MIKE
(Whispering to himself)
It's not about the destination. It's about the journey and the people we meet along the way.

FADE OUT.
